URI transfers include progress/cancellation; media selection/capture/sharing and capability diagnostics request permissions only on explicit actions, never import. Session unhydrated → signed_out | signed_in | mfa_pending; foreground lock orthogonal. Revocation/account switch cancels requests/sockets and clears protected state. Acceptance includes coordinated hydration/rotation/MFA/OAuth, no DOM native bundle, association/origin verification, cancelled transfer and real-device opt-in passkey/biometric checks.

 OFF-01 Encrypted offline persistence and BKG-01 background sync

Persistence opt-in; SQLCipher mandatory, keys in SecureStore, no plaintext fallback. Scope API/project/immutable branch/user; explicit immutable branch required; cache TTL24h. Queue only explicit single-row writes, returning tickets rather than successful server responses. Inserts require supplied PK; update/delete require expected server revision. Persist stable idempotency before send; no automatic uncertain retry after23h from first attempt (server retention24h). Conflict pauses until discard/explicit rebase. Auth/RPC/bulk/file queues online-only.

Queue queued → sending → acknowledged | retry_wait | conflict | needs_review | discarded; server remains authoritative. Signout wipes protected cache/queues/sessions/subscriptions. Pause background sockets; foreground revalidate/replay/refetch. Atomic lease coordinates foreground/headless; flush≤20operations/20seconds; request15min interval but OS schedules, not a guarantee. Keys available after first unlock for unattended encrypted sync; optional biometric foreground lock does not gate background keys. Acceptance: encrypted restart/no plaintext, scope/account isolation, leases/crashes, idempotency horizon, conflicts/manual rebase, offline expiry, signout and physical-device scheduling opt-in.

 PSH-01 Installation registration/lifecycle

Use expo-notifications permissions/Expo tokens/responses/channels/badges/local notifications. After explicit permission and validated sign-in auto-upsert against server-derived user, never supplied userId. Multiple devices; one current user per scoped installation. Scope project/immutable branch/native app/EAS project/environment/platform. Raw tokens encrypted, listings masked. Reacquire Expo token after native token change and retry registration on connectivity recovery.

active → opted_out | deregistered | invalid | inactive; sends exclude age≥30days; daily cleanup deletes token values. Only authenticated foreground check-ins update server lastSeenAt, throttled24h; sends/receipts/background do not. Immediate invalidation for DeviceNotRegistered/deleted user/opt-out/deregistration. Online logout deregisters; offline logout retains only installation-revocation credential until acknowledgment, no login/data/register/send rights. Restores/previews never revive registrations/campaigns. Masked lifecycle/campaign history30days. Acceptance: exact30day boundary, rotation/retry, account switch/ownership, encrypted storage, offline revocation rights, restore exclusion, platform/env separation.

 PSH-02 Delivery, API, worker and Studio

Distinct development/staging/production EAS projects and native app IDs; separate iOS/Android Test Lab. Dedicated Node24LTS worker with expo-server-sdk7.2.0, no PGlite mount. APNs/FCM credentials stay in Expo/EAS; Expo access tokens encrypted server-side. Disabled by default; optional Compose service; restricted worker credential and health checks. Configuration contracts QB_PUSH_ENABLED, QB_PUSH_WORKER_TOKEN, QB_PUSH_INTERNAL_API_URL remain proposed until validated implementation exists.

Studio operators/scoped trusted-server sends only; users manage own installations/preferences. Developers test dev/staging; production send and credential changes owner/admin plus existing MFA. 202 campaign ID; drafts/templates, dry-run audience, single installation/user, filtered bulk, UTC schedules, unsent cancellation and explicit failed-recipient retry. Snapshot/deduplicate recipients; recheck current ownership/activity/preferences/environment before each dispatch.

Campaign draft → scheduled/queued → sending → completed | partially_failed | cancelled; recipient pending → accepted → provider_handoff | failed | skipped | unknown. Never claim delivery/read confirmation.≤5000 installations/campaign;≤100messages/batch; shared≤300messages/sec/EAS project;≤6retry attempts/1h. Receipt check after15min,≤1000IDs/batch, before24h expiry; unknown remains distinguishable. Provider guidance: [Expo delivery](https://docs.expo.dev/push-notifications/sending-notifications/).

Add /notifications: Overview, Tokens & Users, Composer, Campaigns, Test Lab, Configuration. Production confirmation, audited token reveal, quotas/receipt timelines/cleanup reports. Typed installation/campaign/receipt SDK/hooks and management preview/send/status/cancel. Default messages use generic text/resource IDs; already handed-off messages cannot be recalled. Acceptance: production MFA/scoped sends, worker role isolation, rate/batch boundaries, replay/ambiguous outcomes, partial failures/receipt expiry, cancellation/schedule/explicit retries, real push only opt-in certification.

 34. Optional WASM capabilities and portability

All four are required in expanded release, but optional at runtime, lazy-loaded browser workers with pinned self-hosted assets. They never replace native server PGlite or become Hermes dependencies. No secrets enter workers; login/CRUD/normal uploads work when unsupported. Single-thread baseline; do not globally enable isolation headers that break OAuth/embeds.

| ID | Library / capability | Required controls and acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WAS-01 | Official SQLite WASM: local SQL/imported SQLite/schema-only synthetic rehearsal | In-memory default; explicit OPFS consent/delete and documented single-owner limits; server rehearsal authoritative. Unsupported/malformed/oversized/cancel and persistence deletion tests. [Persistence guidance](https://www.sqlite.org/wasm/doc/trunk/persistence.md) |
| WAS-02 | jSquash resize/WebP before-upload optimization | Opt-in preview before/after; preserve original; approved formats/input/pixel limits; cancel worker; server MIME/size/checksum authoritative. Malformed image/pixel-bomb/original/cancel tests. |
| WAS-03 | hash-wasm incremental SHA256 | Bounded imported/transfer chunks; optional expected upload checksum verified during server streamed finalization; existing clients/native crypto unchanged. Digest vectors/mismatch/large-file/cancel/legacy tests. |
| WAS-04 | DuckDB-WASM local CSV/JSON/Parquet profiling/query | Registered local files only; reject remote fetch and extension installation; transactional CRUD unaffected. Remote-SQL rejection, malformed file, query/result/time bounds tests. |

Default one active heavy worker/workspace,100MiB imported-file budget,2MiB result budget,10second query/rehearsal limit. Terminate on cancel/timeout; bound engine memory where supported; browser/device limits remain honest. Consent persistence explicitly and delete files/keys on request. Review wrapper and embedded-code licensing/security. Measure cold start, download bytes, peak memory, processing/cancel time and low-end responsiveness; no unmeasured speed claims.

Deferred candidates/adoption criteria: Tree-sitter only for justified structural editor features; RE2-WASM only for user-regex safety with unsupported syntax rejected; Zstandard after measured compression and versioned bounded decompression; ONNX after optional model budgets/device fallback; Extism after resource/capability/tenant isolation proof; Wasmtime only for separately isolated untrusted function service. Do not install these merely to populate a roadmap.

Compatibility certification targets: LinuxAMD64/ARM64 production containers; macOS native development; Windows via WSL2/Docker. Native Windows experimental. Chromium/Firefox/WebKit desktop plus real mobile-browser smoke checks. Native extension failures explicit. No universal every-device promise.

 35. Dependencies, deployment and architecture decisions

Implement in dependency order, not separate release completion: (1)spec/contracts/migrations/capability states/traceability; (2)jobs/streaming/metrics/diagnostics/auth extensions; (3)recovery/security/operations/alerts/query inspection; (4)native/offline/background/push; (5)reviews/previews/webhooks/inbox/realtime/search/WASM; (6)Docs/deployment/packaging/compatibility/full verification.

Update ADRs for durable lease fencing, encrypted stream framing, diagnostics privacy, schema-only previews, separate object recovery, native session/offline isolation, Node push executor, SSRF-safe webhook dispatch and optional worker WASM. Deployment instructions must specify private scratch/disk budgets, separate off-node destinations/key custody, push-off default/private executor connectivity, operator-provisioned EAS/association documents and physical-device certification. Existing Docker/env flows remain valid.

 36. Requirements-to-tests traceability and completion policy

[The implementation ledger](/docs/roadmap/expanded-release) records concrete test files/evidence and missing gates. An acceptance ID is not passing just because a test filename is proposed. Unit/mocked behavior does not certify external providers or physical devices.

| Requirement | Required acceptance evidence |
| --- | --- |
| REC-01 | Off-node/drill/inventory/retention/freshness, corruption/key/object gaps, unchanged alias, legacy restore |
| SEC-01 | Actual engine fixture isolation and old/prospective policies, findings/ack expiry, privilege input regression |
| OPS-01 / ALERT-01 | Histograms/label privacy/retention, scoped summaries, threshold/dedup/cooldown/ack/recovery and delivery failures |
| STR-01 | Memory/backpressure/cancel/checksum/quota/concurrency/crash cleanup, authenticated v2/legacy archives |
| DOC-01 | Redacted readonly checks/probes/exit codes; no inadvertent email/push/write probes |
| QIN-01 | Policy query plans without values, bounded summaries and reviewed-only index suggestions |
| REV-01 / PRE-01 | Stale review/digest, unsafe SQL, type compilation, fixture/secret exclusions, fresh realm, quotas/TTL/fencing |
| JOB-01 / WHK-01 | Crash/reopen/dedup/expired leases/fenced results/dead letter/replay/checkpoint atomicity; signatures/rotation/auth projection/SSRF DNS/IPv6 |
| LAB-01 / WAS-01–04 | Local-only inputs/remote SQL rejected/budgets/cancellation/unsupported fallback/persistence deletion/core unaffected; measured budgets |
| RTD-01 / SEA-01 | Replay/revocation/identity/redaction; no cross-user search counts/snippets/hidden columns; index invalidation |
| NAT-01 / OFF-01 / BKG-01 | Metro/declarations/legacy browser, coordinated sessions/encrypted restart/scopes/conflicts/idempotency horizon/signout/leases; device opt-in |
| PSH-01 / PSH-02 | User-derived token ownership/rotation/exact30day/offline logout/environment/MFA/worker limits/receipts/crash/cancel; real push opt-in |
| COMP-01 | Repository/browser/CLI/Compose/build/SDK-consumer/skill gates, declared OS/architectures/browsers plus opt-in device evidence |

Completion requires every expanded feature and acceptance evidence. Run bun run typecheck, bun run check, browser/CLI/Compose/packed SDK consumers/build, skill:refresh, skill:check, and skill:test before packaging. Add Firefox/WebKit and declared platform jobs; skipped gates stay explicit. Physical passkey/biometric/background/real push are explicit opt-in certification, not mocks.

 37. Authorization boundary

This implementation does not authorize external deployment, EAS credential provisioning, store submissions, production notifications, npm publication, automatic recovery cutover, multi-region operation, vector/AI services or integrated object-byte backup. Tests use isolated fixtures. Do not read/log live keys or erase unrelated working-tree changes. Product version remains0.1.0 until a separate authorized release change.

 Database engine conversion contract

The platform uses embedded PGlite PostgreSQL for the catalog, branch data, auth, storage metadata, jobs and policy simulation. New SQL is PostgreSQL; SQLite SQL compatibility is not a runtime feature. REST/SDK scalar representations remain 0/1 booleans, UTC timestamps, JSON text, base64 binary values and strings for unsafe integers.

qb db migrate-engine --from sqlite --to pglite --data-dir SOURCE --output-dir DESTINATION [--check] requires stopped writers and exclusive ownership, including the legacy SQLite ownership lock. Paths must not overlap and the destination must be empty. Preflight inventories every referenced branch, rejects custom views/triggers, virtual/generated objects, unsafe defaults/constraints and mixed-type values, and reports blockers rather than omitting data. Convert ordinary tables, supported defaults/constraints/indexes and values, then verify row counts, canonical content hashes, foreign keys, catalog references and identity sequences. Historical migration SQL/checksums remain unchanged; engine migration baselines are separate. Preserve encrypted keys, credentials, sessions, durable jobs/checkpoints and archive bytes; do not produce new row events during copying. Preserve source databases and original key custody. Publish engine.json only after complete validation. Switching QB_DATA_DIR is a separately scheduled activation; rollback after accepting writes requires reconciliation.

Legacy branch/control archive restoration uses the same converter and keeps its recovery sanitization/revocation contracts. Control swaps have a recovery journal and encrypted rollback snapshot. The original encrypted archive format remains readable; new snapshots authenticate PGlite version metadata. PostgreSQL wire access, new vector/search features and browser/native database accelerators remain outside this migration.

Historical SQLite/Linux throughput and native-extension evidence predates this engine migration. Current PGlite validation must be reported separately; Linux/Compose requires a working Docker daemon and is not implied by local macOS results.

Errors and limits
text:
Errors and limits

 Error contract

SDK methods throw QBError with code, message, status, retryable and optional details. API failures include a request ID. Preserve it when reporting a failure.

| Status | Meaning | Application response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | Validation or unsupported input | Correct the request |
| 401 | Missing, expired or wrong-realm credential | Authenticate again |
| 403 | Policy or organization denial | Check permissions |
| 404 | Missing or invisible resource | Treat as unavailable |
| 409 | Revision, checksum or idempotency conflict | Refetch/reconcile |
| 413 | Body or object size limit | Reduce the payload |
| 429 | Rate quota | Back off |
| 503 | Owner or external dependency unavailable | Retry eligible operations |

 Default bounds

Read pages default to 50 and cap at 500 rows. Atomic inserts cap at 100 rows. Query filters cap at 30, membership values at 100 and policy nesting at 12. Branch queues cap at 64 requests and active owners at 32 per API instance.

The default database and total reserved object quotas are 1 GiB per branch. Studio enters those two limits in MB. Project configuration stores quotas.databaseBytes and quotas.storageBytes in bytes, plus quotas.requestsPerMinute, with optimistic If-Match updates. The default rate quota is 600 requests per minute per credential; the process keeps at most 10,000 credential buckets. Database admission includes the main file and WAL; a final admitted transaction may cross its threshold. Object intents reserve space before upload.

Realtime connections cap at 100 per project and 256 per process. Realtime frames cap at 64 KiB. Storage uploads cap at 100 MiB, with smaller bucket-specific limits. Privileged SQL console results cap at 500 rows.

Database pages and their expanded relationships share a conservative 2 MiB serialization budget, measured in PGlite before loading row values. Reduce the projection or page size after RESULT_TOO_LARGE. Events with oversized row images require a fresh snapshot instead of replay. The API admits four concurrent uploads and two snapshots; additional work receives retryable TRANSFER_BUSY or BACKUP_BUSY. Object listings currently return at most 500 ready objects.

 Safe retry

The SDK retries bounded safe reads and explicitly idempotent writes. A timeout may leave commit status uncertain. Reconcile using the same idempotency key; do not assume cancellation undoes a committed database transaction.

title: Compatibility and implementation status
text:
Compatibility and implementation status

 Verified locally

Bun 1.4.2, Elysia, worker-owned PGlite, Better Auth realm isolation, MFA enrollment/challenges, generated TypeScript, React Strict Mode lifecycle tests, realtime reconnect, S3-compatible storage and encrypted restore have executable tests in this repository. Consult VERIFICATION.md for the actual build/browser/Linux results and environment.

 Deployment certification

Google and GitHub adapters require your registered credentials and live callback testing. Production TLS, SMTP delivery outside Mailpit, encrypted disks, external S3 backends and sustained performance/recovery objectives require checks in your deployment. No scale, RPO or RTO targets are advertised as measured achievements.

 Measured baseline

On 6 October 2026, a Linux ARM64 container on an Apple M5 Pro host ran a one-million-row ownership-policy workload with WAL/FULL durability. With four CPU equivalents and an 8 GiB container memory limit, 1,000 indexed reads at 100 requests/second measured p95 4.29 ms; 100 writes at 25 writes/second measured p95 8.97 ms. All requests and authorized row events succeeded. Event delivery measured p95 250.18 ms from request start, including commit time. Snapshot and validated isolated restore took 1.393 and 1.820 seconds.

The temporary filesystem was Docker OverlayFS on the local VM disk. The shared VM reported 8,317,267,968 bytes of physical memory; the container's 8 GiB setting was a configured ceiling. These short virtualized runs do not certify sustained scale, multi-tenant fairness, power-loss recovery or production disks. [Download the raw result and environment metadata](/benchmark.json). The reproducible source is scripts/benchmark.ts in the repository.

 Database engine transition

The current engine is PGlite 0.5.10 with Kysely 0.29.6 on Bun. Historical SQLite/Linux throughput and extension results above do not establish PGlite performance or compatibility. New regression tests cover PGlite transactions, conversion, authentication and archive recovery. Platform-specific gates must be rerun for the new engine.

Vector/search product APIs remain planned. Installing PGlite does not enable pgvector, PostgreSQL wire access, Supabase compatibility or browser database workflows.

 Current boundaries

Public APIs support ordinary tables, scalar filters, keyset pagination, atomic batches, upsert, registered foreign-key relationships, relationship existence policies and reviewed structured RPC. Relationship expansion is one level deep and capped at three relationships, 100 parent rows and 50 child rows. Policies reject recursive relationship cycles.

Storage has owner/private and public-read rules with bounded disk-staged streaming gateway uploads with optional SHA-256. Custom storage-policy expressions, resumable transfers and image processing are planned. Management tokens grant selected projects; server service keys require explicit branch/table/method scopes. SQL developer privileges are trusted schema administration.

The deployment owns all writable databases from one API process. It does not provide distributed owners, automatic failover, SQLCipher, point-in-time recovery or external OAuth certification. Metrics cover HTTP traffic, active owners and disk capacity; contract-labeled private latency histograms are implemented, while the full Operations Dashboard, alerts, distributed tracing and advanced feature metrics remain incomplete.

 Supported clients

The initial supported application tracks are React 19 and Vanilla JavaScript browser ESM. SSR must create a client and QueryClient per request; browser effects start after hydration. Other framework adapters remain deferred; React Native/offline/background/push are required by the expanded specification but are not implemented or certified yet.

 Expanded compatibility targets and evidence boundaries

Linux AMD64/ARM64 containers, macOS development, Windows through WSL2/Docker, Chromium/Firefox/WebKit and real mobile-browser smoke checks are the expanded targets—not an assertion all gates pass today. Native Windows remains experimental until equivalent gates pass. Current browser regression evidence is Chromium; do not infer Firefox/WebKit or real-device certification from it.

The current foundation has executable tests for encrypted/fenced durable jobs, policy-fixture isolation, revision guards, streaming archives/legacy restore, upload checksums/cancellation, redacted Doctor output and private histograms. Test coverage is not a substitute for running those tests on a deployment. Native/push/WASM, full recovery/Advisor/operations and developer workflows remain [incomplete](/docs/roadmap/expanded-release). Physical passkey, biometric, background and real-push gates are opt-in and are not proven by mocks.

Expanded release specification 1.1

Specification1.1 does not change product version0.1.0. The expanded release is under development, not available as a complete feature set. The repository development specification and docs/expanded-release-status.md are the normative requirements and implementation ledger.

 Implemented foundations

Durable jobs live in private branch tables within existing owners: encrypted payloads, deduplicated submissions, fenced leases, bounded retries, attempt history, cancellation and explicit dead-letter replay. Management routes expose metadata, not payloads or lease credentials. Push replay is blocked until recipient-aware campaigns exist. Studio /jobs now provides private metadata, attempt history, pagination and explicit replay/cancel confirmations. Experimental [database webhooks](/docs/studio/webhooks) now add atomic outbox checkpoints, scoped/current-policy projections, signed exact-byte deliveries, rotation/retries and pinned SSRF-safe HTTPS. Notification and alert services remain pending.

Policy simulation now supports synthetic fixtures and real-engine SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE without modifying production rows. Legacy read tests remain compatible and cannot enable service bypass with request fields. DELETE forwards revision guards like PATCH. Experimental [Security Advisor](/docs/studio/security-advisor) adds bounded metadata findings, remediation, expiring evidence-bound acknowledgments and Studio /security. Static checks are not a security audit.

Both application and management uploads stream through private disk staging, with incremental SHA256 and optional expected checksum. Branch archives use authenticated streamed v2 framing; legacy branch archives remain readable. Control-catalog archives now use self-contained authenticated streamed v2 metadata, with bounded legacy recovery, offline rollback and revoked restored capabilities.

Private metrics include cumulative latency histograms with contract-derived bounded labels. qb doctor adds read-only redacted local checks and an explicitly requested readiness probe. Configuration presence is not connectivity or provider certification.

 Required before expanded release completion

Recovery Center; full Security Advisor/simulator acceptance; Operations Dashboard and alerts; full streaming acceptance; live Deployment Doctor probes; Query Inspector; Schema Change Review; expiring schema/fixture-only previews; full webhook crash/load/compatibility certification; Local Data Lab; identity-aware Realtime Debugger; permission-aware PostgreSQL full-text search.

Native SDK, SQLCipher caches/queued writes, SecureStore sessions, OAuth/passkeys, optional media/background capabilities and the complete Expo push lifecycle/campaign/toolkit/Node-worker integration remain required, not implemented by the job foundation.

All four browser WASM integrations remain required: SQLite WASM, jSquash resize/WebP, hash-wasm SHA256 and DuckDB-WASM. They are optional/lazy-loaded capabilities, never server PGlite replacements or required for login/CRUD.

 Verification and deployment boundaries

The full release requires compatibility gates, legacy consumer/archive tests, policy isolation, crash/lease behavior, bounded transfer measurements, SSRF/signatures, encrypted native restart/conflicts, push lifecycle/environment/MFA/receipts and local-worker budget/cancellation tests. Physical passkey/biometric/background/real-push checks are explicit opt-in certification. Mocks do not certify providers/devices.

No deployment, external publication, EAS credentials, production notifications, automatic cutover, multi-region services or integrated object-byte backup is implied. Object-store backup/versioning and master-key custody remain separately managed operator responsibilities.

 Feature-by-feature development status

| Required feature | What exists now | Remaining accepted scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recovery Center | Encrypted branch/control snapshots; isolated restore and retention. | Encrypted off-node destinations/inventory, freshness alerts, scheduled isolated drills and separate database/object/key verification reports. No automatic cutover or integrated object-copy backup. |
| Security Advisor + Policy Simulator | Real-engine simulator; bounded grant/exposure/bucket/key-age/MFA findings, evidence/remediation, expiring acknowledgment and Advisor UI. | Full relationship/type/constraint matrix, hard scratch execution budget and broader security/compatibility acceptance. No automatic fixes. |
| Operations Dashboard | Private request counters, contract-labeled latency histograms, owner/disk basics. | Authorized latency/queue/restarts/WAL/outbox/maintenance/backup/delivery summaries with bounded labels/retention and redacted data. |
| Bounded streaming transfers | Private disk-staged uploads, checksum/cancellation and streamed branch/control v2 archives with legacy recovery. | Full expanded stress/restart/concurrency evidence and remaining transfer validation gates. Resumable multipart remains deferred. |
| Deployment Doctor | Read-only redacted CLI inventory and explicitly requested readiness GET. | Runtime/ownership/provider/worker/destination/native diagnostics; explicitly invoked scoped write/mail/push probes. |
| Query Inspector | Existing trusted SQL console; not an inspector. | Normalized slow queries, owner-generated plans including policies, schema-based index suggestions and reviewed comparisons; no values or automatic indexes. |
| Schema Change Review | Migration/backup path and Schema Visualizer. | Destructive diffs, isolated safe rehearsal, exposure/policy review, generated type checks and approvals bound to the base schema version. |
| Disposable Preview Environments | Isolated restore exists; not a preview service. | Schema/policy-only fresh-identity forks with reviewed fixtures, quotas, default 72-hour/max-seven-day TTL and fenced cleanup. Never clone users/tokens/jobs/destinations; no merge/promotion. |
| Durable Webhooks + Job Inbox | Encrypted queue, atomic checkpoints, scoped/current-policy projections, signed exact-byte deliveries/rotation/retries, pinned HTTPS/SSRF checks and Studio controls. | Full crash/queue/load/cross-platform certification and downstream operational alerts. Local TLS tests are not production receiver certification. |
| Local Data Lab | Specification only. | Explicit local imports, schema preview/query/profile/export, opt-in persistence/deletion and bounded local workers; no silent uploads or remote SQL fetch. |
| Realtime Debugger | Current SDK lifecycle/reconnect/replay and basic Studio guidance. | Metadata-only tracing, gaps/resync/latency and identity-scoped application debug sessions. |
| Permission-aware Search | No application search API/collection service. | Registered PostgreSQL full-text collections over exposed allowed text, transactional indexes, policy-filtered results/counts/snippets, deterministic pagination and schema-change invalidation. Docs search is unrelated. |

 Operational alerts

Planned Studio/email/signed-webhook alerts reuse the mail adapter and durable delivery facility. They need configured recipients/destinations, deduplication, acknowledgment, cooldown and recovery notifications. Defaults cover stale backups, disk pressure, sustained queue saturation, maintenance and delivery-worker failure. Current auth mail is not this alert service.

 Native, notifications and browser accelerators

Read the dedicated [native/offline/background/push requirements](/docs/roadmap/native-push) and [WASM/Data Lab requirements](/docs/roadmap/wasm). These pages describe accepted contracts without presenting unsupported runnable SDK methods. All remain required, not completed by the job foundation.

 Dependency order and acceptance traceability

The implementation order is specification/contracts, shared jobs/streaming/metrics/authorization, production confidence, native/push, developer workflows/WASM, then full documentation/packaging/compatibility verification. Completing one stage does not satisfy the overall release.

The [specification 1.1](/docs/reference/development-spec) includes purpose, workflows, authorization, API/SDK/state/configuration/limits/failure/compatibility contracts and requirements-to-tests traceability. Require real crash/negative/isolation tests, legacy consumers/archives, bounded transfers, signatures/SSRF, preview secret exclusion, policy-aware search, encrypted native restart, exact push cleanup boundaries and worker cancellation/budgets. Generated capability status remains available in the [API reference](/docs/reference/management-api).

title: Feature roadmap
text:
Feature roadmap

 P0 foundation

Organizations, projects, primary databases, migrations, protected REST access, application auth, row events, basic S3 storage, SDKs, CLI, audit records and backups form the foundation. The repository verification report tracks whether each release gate has passed.

 P1 developer platform

Planned work includes GraphQL with REST policy parity, magic links/OTP, more certified social providers, database webhooks, presence/broadcast channels, resumable uploads, transforms and general snapshot branching. Approved relationship-existence policies are already implemented in P0.

Vector search, provider-neutral AI, permission-aware ingestion, isolated Bun functions and hosted OAuth MCP require additional native/runtime certification. They are not available simply because their navigation item exists.

 P2 advanced operations

SSO, OAuth identity-provider behavior, replicas, CDN integration, analytics buckets, regional placement, RAG workflows, Deno functions and Terraform follow separate authorization and recovery gates.

 Architecture baseline

Read the [complete development specification](/docs/reference/development-spec) for platform design, requested capabilities, phased contracts and threat-model requirements. It is a baseline specification, not a claim that every phase is implemented.

 Specification 1.1 supersedes the earlier phase assignments

The [expanded release](/docs/roadmap/expanded-release) requires all twelve production/developer workflows, native/offline/background/push and four optional browser WASM integrations as one release. Sections 31–37 of the [generated development specification](/docs/reference/development-spec) take precedence over conflicting historical P0/P1/P2 assignments. Broad GraphQL/AI/connectors/distributed ownership remain deferred candidates. Product version is still 0.1.0; an early foundation is not release completion.

title: Native SDK and push requirements
text:
Native SDK and push requirements

 Status: required, not implemented

@qb-flex/react-native, native adapters, automatic polyfills, encrypted offline queues, background synchronization and Expo push are not currently available. Browser SDKs are the implemented tracks. The accepted scope is part of specification 1.1, not a separate completed release or npm availability announcement.

 Native foundation

The planned async native client shares provider/hooks and adds optional background, notifications and media entrypoints. React DOM must be optional, React external and exports Metro-compatible, with no eager browser WebAuthn code in Hermes bundles. Importing the SDK must not request permissions.

The specified certification baseline is Expo SDK 57 (expo@57.0.26), React Native 0.86.3 and React 19.2.3 with Hermes/New Architecture, including bare RN with Expo modules. These are requested pins, not certified integrations. SecureStore-coordinated Better Auth sessions, rotation, TOTP/OAuth callbacks and native passkeys require real device/association validation.

Missing URL, secure UUID, abort composition, UTF-8 and base64url capabilities must be supplied without replacing working host implementations or using insecure random/DOM emulation. Optional features include biometric foreground lock, URI transfers with progress/cancellation, media selection/capture/sharing and capability diagnostics.

 Offline and background contract

Persistence is opt-in and requires SQLCipher encryption with SecureStore keys—no plaintext fallback. Scope is API/project/immutable branch/user; an offline client must choose an explicit branch ID. Cache expiry defaults to 24 hours.

Queued single-row writes return tickets, not successful server results. Inserts require supplied keys; updates/deletes require expected server revisions. Persist idempotency before delivery, stop uncertain automatic retries 23 hours after the first attempt and pause conflicts for discard or explicit rebase. Auth, RPC, bulk and file-upload queues remain online-only.

Signout clears protected caches, mutations, sessions and subscriptions. Foreground/headless sync share an atomic lease, with 20-operation/20-second flush bounds. The requested 15-minute background interval is subject to OS scheduling. Sockets pause in background and revalidate/replay/refetch on foreground. Background keys remain available after first unlock; biometric foreground lock does not gate unattended sync.

 Push lifecycle

The proposed implementation uses expo-notifications and a dedicated Node 24 LTS expo-server-sdk@7.2.0 executor without a SQLite mount. No such executor/Compose service exists yet. APNs/FCM credentials stay with Expo/EAS; provider access tokens are encrypted server secrets.

After permission and validated sign-in, installations register against the server-derived user. Multiple devices are supported with one current user per scoped installation. Scope includes project, immutable branch, application, EAS project, environment and platform. Raw tokens are encrypted and listings masked. Token rotation/connectivity recovery trigger reacquisition and registration.

Authenticated foreground check-ins update activity at most once daily. Sends, receipts and background jobs do not count. Exclude tokens at 30 days of inactivity and remove token values during daily cleanup. Immediately invalidate opt-out, deleted users, deregistration and DeviceNotRegistered. Online logout deregisters; offline logout may retain only a restricted installation-revocation credential until acknowledgment. Restores/previews must never revive registrations or pending campaigns.

 Studio and delivery scope

The planned /notifications workspace contains Overview, Tokens & Users, Composer, Campaigns, platform-separated Test Lab and Configuration. Distinct EAS projects/application identifiers separate development/staging/production. Production sends and credential changes require owner/admin plus existing MFA.

Planned tools include drafts/templates, dry-run audiences, single-installation/user and filtered bulk sends, UTC scheduling, unsent cancellation, explicit failed-recipient retry, masked tokens with audited reveal, quotas, receipt timelines and cleanup reports. Trusted-server send credentials are explicitly scoped; end users manage only their own installations/preferences.

Campaign submission returns 202 plus an ID. Snapshot/deduplicate audiences and recheck ownership, activity, preferences and environment before dispatch. Limits: 5,000 installations/campaign, 100 messages/provider batch, shared 300 messages/second/EAS project and six attempts within one hour. Check receipts after 15 minutes, at most 1,000 IDs/batch and before 24-hour expiry. States distinguish accepted/provider handoff/failed/skipped/unknown—not confirmed delivery or reading. Keep masked lifecycle/campaign history for 30 days.

 Certification gates

Require encrypted restart, account isolation/switching, conflict/idempotency, offline logout, exact inactivity boundaries, token rotation, environment separation, production MFA and receipt failures. Physical passkey, biometric, OS background and real push checks are explicit opt-in gates. Current job storage/restricted worker credentials alone do not implement or certify any of these workflows.

title: Optional WASM tooling requirements
text:
Optional WASM tooling requirements

 Status: required, not integrated

These four integrations are required by specification 1.1 but are not installed as working QB Flex capabilities yet. WASM is an optional browser accelerator, not a replacement for server PGlite, server authorization or a native Hermes dependency. Login, CRUD and normal uploads must work without it.

| Library | Planned workflow | Required guardrails |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SQLite WASM | Inspect explicitly imported databases; local SQL and schema-only rehearsal with synthetic fixtures. | In-memory default; explicit OPFS consent/delete, documented single-owner concurrency; server rehearsal remains authoritative. |
| jSquash resize/WebP | Opt-in pre-upload optimization with before/after preview. | Preserve original; bound input/pixels/formats; cancellation; server MIME/size/checksum validation remains authoritative. |
| hash-wasm | Incremental SHA-256 for large browser imports/transfers. | Bounded chunks and workers; optional expected checksum only; native crypto remains the server baseline. |
| DuckDB-WASM | Local CSV/JSON/Parquet analysis, profiling and bounded result export. | Register local files only; block remote fetching and extension installs; never part of transactional CRUD. |

The existing upload SDK already accepts an optional checksum and the server verifies it before S3 persistence; that does not mean the hash-wasm browser worker exists. Current Schema Visualizer is also not a SQLite WASM playground.

 Local Data Lab contract

Explicitly imported files stay on the device; nothing uploads automatically. The planned separate workspace includes schema preview, bounded queries, profiling and result export. Default storage is ephemeral; persistence requires consent and an explicit delete control. No management credentials, S3 secrets or master keys enter workers.

 Budgets and portability

Allow one active heavy worker per workspace, at most 100 MiB imported files and 2 MiB query results, with a ten-second query/rehearsal timeout. Terminate on cancellation/timeout, bound engine memory where supported and report device/browser limits honestly.

Lazy-load and self-host pinned runtime assets. Review wrapper and embedded-library licenses/advisories. Single-threaded operation is the baseline; do not globally enable isolation headers that break OAuth or embeds. Unsupported devices receive an actionable explanation and working core workflows.

Measure cold startup, download bytes, processing time, memory, cancellation and low-end responsiveness before claiming a performance gain. Acceptance includes malformed/oversized inputs, remote-access rejection, budgets, cancellation, persistence deletion and unchanged core behavior.

 Deferred candidates

Tree-sitter requires a justified structural editor and SQLite-compatible grammar. RE2-WASM requires a real user-regex use case and explicit unsupported-syntax rejection. Zstandard needs compression benchmarks, decompressed-size bounds and versioned recovery. ONNX Runtime Web needs justified local models, download budgets and unsupported-device handling. Extism/Wasmtime require certified isolation, capability/resource limits and runtime patching before untrusted functions. These are not installed dependencies or expanded-release promises.
